The voltage-drop approximation ΔV≒√3·I·(R cosθ+X sinθ) is the standard form for a three-phase line, and the cause-and-effect reasoning is correct. Extending the line length (4) increases R and X roughly in proportion to length, which makes the voltage drop larger, so it is not a voltage-maintenance measure.

The reasons given for the correct statements are specific to each option and correct: (1) sending-end voltage adjustment with LRT/LRA, combined with LDC where needed; (2) a phase-advancing capacitor reduces reactive current, and with the active current I·cosθ unchanged, the I·X·sinθ component falls; (3) a thicker conductor lowers R; (5) placing the transformer at the load center shortens the low-voltage lines.
